snippet.description:

snippet.title: Newsom Says California to Sue Over Trump’s Tariffs
snippet.description:
California Governor Gavin Newsom said his state is suing to halt Donald Trump’s tariffs, setting up a high-stakes legal challenge to the president’s landmark effort to overhaul global trade.

The state will file a complaint Wednesday in San Francisco federal court challenging Trump’s use of emergency powers to enact broad tariffs against Mexico, China and Canada, according to a statement issued by Newsom’s office. Officials cited harm to consumers and businesses in the world’s fifth-largest economy.

Newsom, a Democrat who’s considered a likely candidate to run for president in 2028, and California Attorney General Rob Bonta will seek a court order to immediately block the levies. “President Trump’s unlawful tariffs are wreaking chaos on California families, businesses, and our economy — driving up prices and threatening jobs,” Newsom said.

“Instead of focusing on California’s rampant crime, homelessness, and unaffordability, Gavin Newsom is spending his time trying to block President Trump’s historic efforts to finally address the national emergency of our country’s persistent goods trade deficits,” a White House spokesman said in a statement.

snippet.title: '100 percent' chance of tariff deal with EU says Trump | DW News
snippet.description:
Italian Prime Minister Georgia Meloni has met with US Vice President JD Vance in Italy, just a day after meeting with President Donald Trump at the White House.

Trump said there was a "100 percent" chance that the US would reach a deal with the European Union on his tariffs. There's currently a 10 percent import levy on all imports from the EU. 

Meloni's charm offensive comes as the right-wing Italian leader has positioned herself as something of a Trump whisperer and a bridge builder between the US and Europe.

DW spoke to political scientist Antonio Zotti from the Catholic University of the Sacred Heart in Milan about Meloni's visit. He shared his insights on Meloni and Trump's close relationship.

Riccardo Alcaro from the Insitute for International Affairs, a thinktank based in Rome also joined us. Alcaro explained that while Meloni may have won warm words from Trump, any gains could be elusive under such an unpredictable administration.

snippet.title: ‘Solvency issues’: Xi Jinping cannot ‘wait out’ Donald Trump’s tariffs
snippet.description:
Kaiyuan Capital Managing Director Brock Silvers says Chinese President Xi Jinping cannot “wait out” US President Donald Trump’s four-year presidency.

“I think it will be very difficult to wait Trump out for a full four years – to use an old Chinese saying, heaven is high, and the end of four years is far away,” Mr Silvers said. 

“I don’t think that Xi Jinping can just wait this out, I think there are problems in the Chinese economy that are going to have to be dealt with.

“Not only is there real solvency issues across a number of key sectors, but we also see just sort of lower growth despite the claims of 5.4 per cent.”

snippet.title: US-Japan tariff talks yield no breakthrough even as Trump hails 'big progress'
snippet.description: Japanese Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba has warned that trade negotiations with the US will not be easy, after discussions between Washington and Tokyo yielded no real breakthrough. US President Donald Trump, though, said officials made "big progress" in talks. Japan wants a review of US tariffs, including the 25% on auto imports that are already in effect. A separate 24% duty on Japanese goods has been paused for now. Nina-Maria Potts reports from Washington DC.
